messages.subject: scale_hue vs colorspace
parts:
Dear all

I would expect the fill colours of the following plots to be
identical, as the arguments are the same, but they are not.
Am I missing something or is it that scale_fill_hue is not directly
compatible with colorspace rainbow_hcl function?

Thanks.

===
library(ggplot2)
library(colorspace)

df <- data.frame(x=letters[1:4], y=1)
p <- qplot(data=df, x, y, geom="bar", stat="identity", fill=x)
p1 <- p + scale_fill_hue(h=c(30, 300), c = 50, l = 70) + opts
(title="fill_hue")

colours <- rainbow_hcl(4, c = 50, l = 70, start = 30, end = 300)
p2 <- p + scale_fill_manual (values=colours) + opts
(title="fill_manual")

vplayout <- function(x, y)
viewport(layout.pos.row=x, layout.pos.col=y)
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout=grid.layout(2,1)))
print(p1, vp=vplayout(1,1))
print(p2, vp=vplayout(2,1))

--
learnr.wordpress.com

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: scale_hue vs colorspace
parts:
It's because scale_fill_hue generates n + 1 colours between start and
end and then drops the last colour. That's the best method I could
come up with for when you have n colours spanning 0 to 360, but it's
not quite right when you restrict the range of the hues.

Maybe when start and end are equal (mod 360), I should subtract 360/n
from the end point.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: scale_hue vs colorspace
parts:
As you say, it seems that rainbow_hcl uses a slightly different
calculation logic, maybe scale_fill_hue could be updated to use the
same algorithm?

>rainbow_hcl
function (n, c = 50, l = 70, start = 0, end = 360 * (n - 1)/n,
gamma = 2.4, fixup = TRUE, ...)
{
if (n > 0)
hex(polarLUV(L = l, C = c, H = seq(start, end, length = n)),
gamma = gamma, fixup = fixup, ...)
else character(0)
}

--
http://learnr.wordpress.com/
